analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek passes several of my quantitative tests — P/E of 12.8x, D/E of 0.20, and a decade of unbroken earnings — but at INR 1,746 the price sits essentially at its Graham Number (~INR 1,682), leaving no meaningful margin of safety. A disciplined investor must wait for Mr. Market to offer a genuine discount before committing capital.
key_strengths: 10-year unbroken earnings record with net profit CAGR of 32.5% — exactly the kind of proven earning power I require
Debt/Equity of 0.20 and interest coverage ~18x (EBIT 586 Cr / finance cost 32 Cr) — balance sheet is conservatively financed
Free cash flow positive every year (5/5), INR 515 Cr in 2026 — earnings are real, not accounting fiction
key_risks: P/B of 2.02 breaches my 2.0 ceiling — the market is pricing in goodwill from the INR 719 Cr acquisition spend in 2023, which I treat with deep suspicion
Borrowings nearly doubled from 273 Cr (2021) to 583 Cr (2025) before partially reversing — rising finance costs (4 Cr → 44 Cr peak) bear watching
IT services revenue is entirely dependent on discretionary enterprise spending cycles; a client spending freeze or currency headwind (UK, US exposure) can rapidly compress margins
red_flags: Price at Graham Number (~1,682) with no margin of safety — I never buy at fair value, only at a discount to it
Large 2023 acquisition (investing outflow -719 Cr) likely inflated intangible assets; book value may overstate true liquidation value
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Mastek is a rare technology business that a quantitative screen actually does not reject outright. Its P/E of 12.8x is comfortably below my 15x ceiling, its debt is trivial (D/E 0.20), interest is covered eighteen times over, and operating cash flow has been positive in every one of the last five years — culminating in INR 515 Cr of free cash flow in 2026. A nine-year net profit CAGR of 32.5% is the kind of proven earning power that earns my attention. Computing the Graham Number: EPS ≈ INR 130 (404 Cr profit / ~3.1 Cr shares) × BVPS ≈ INR 965 (2,992 Cr equity / ~3.1 Cr shares) yields sqrt(22.5 × 130 × 965) ≈ INR 1,682 — the stock trades at INR 1,746, essentially at par with fair value. I do not buy at fair value; I require a discount of at minimum 30–40%.

The P/B of 2.02 is a second disqualifier: it barely crosses my 2.0 red-flag threshold and likely reflects goodwill from the large 2023 acquisition (investing outflow of 719 Cr in that year). In a liquidation scenario, intangibles evaporate and the true asset backing would be considerably lower than stated equity. Promoter holding at only 35.8% is modest, and the company does not appear to return meaningful cash to shareholders via dividends — further reducing the yield cushion I insist upon. Mastek is a solid, well-run business, but "solid" and "cheap" are two different things. I would revisit seriously below INR 1,200 — a price that would restore the margin of safety the intelligent investor must demand.
